headToHead.voiceNote: Cover the names and Vera is known by status shape: complaint as boast, complicity assumed, the repeated word that flips, two-word orders. Ours is known mostly by vocabulary (Up Next, Skip Intro, subscription, recommend). Strip the UI nouns and 'Bowling. You'll say you've never been. You own the shoes.' or 'You read the last page first and then cry at it anyway, on the bus.' could be Crumb. Crumb and Vex share the dry, all-knowing, judging register, and the bank doesn't separate them. Bar wins voice.
headToHead.constructionNote: Our top 12 are tight. 'which I also found' and 'I'm a subscription' use the bar's repeat-and-flip exactly, and nobody's line explains itself. But four of the twelve use the same staccato three-fragment rhythm (X. Y. Z.), and the pyramid self-reference carries three of them. Vera's best are also well built, and her long lines are prompts, not jokes. Tie.
headToHead.quotableNote: 'step three is me', 'I'm usually the list', 'Goodbye, Egypt' and 'Skip Intro. {rival} was the intro.' would clip. Vera's 'my career on not dating losers like you', 'Right. Now.' and the cattle prod are as clippable and carry more attitude per word. Tie, and only because ours were picked from 137.

Repeats: the same joke for Prince twice (roast: 'Since I started showing Prince to grandmothers, the bingo hall has become a monarchy.'; wingman: 'Prince is wonderful with children; I showed him to a primary school and they've declared a republic.'), and twice for Brock (an alarm into the canal; an app that shouts at monks). 'in a hat' twice: 'I'll recommend you someone better, and it's me again, but in a hat.' and 'I've rigged your phone lines so every caller tonight is me in a different hat.' Six of ten guess/fear lines open on '{star}', against 'do not open two lines the same way'.
biggestGap: The punchlines are arbitrary nouns you could swap out (pelican, heron, melon, ladle, ladders, kayaks, spoon, grout, gate, dentist), not turns the setup forces. Vera's turns reuse the setup's own word or take it literally ('my career... my career on not dating losers'), and ours do that only in our best lines ('which I also found', 'I'm a subscription', 'I'm usually the list'). Next pass: swap each line's closing noun for another random noun, and if the line still works, rewrite it so the last words come from the line's own first half or from Vex's own wants, and cap the quirky-object closer at one line in five.
